correctness.rationale: The pairwise difference and coordinate constraints jointly make the one-dimensional intervals for the diagonal shift intersect, giving the stated box-plus-segment support width. Factor a standard Gaussian as radius times uniform direction: the absolute product expectation of two projections with unit normals of correlation r is g(r)/d, since the independent squared radius has mean d. Integrating the Gaussian sign-correlation formula from r=0 gives g. The squared box term uses r=0 and 1, and the mixed term uses r=1/sqrt(d); subtracting the squared means yields all three variance coefficients. The joint CLT for (|G|-mu,G^2-1,G) has Gaussian third coordinate independent of the first two by parity; normalizing the radius changes the box term to X−mu Y/2 with variance 1−3/pi, while the diagonal tends to |H|. The gamma ratio justifies exact centering, including for varying cant and at both limiting endpoints. The ell sqrt(d) Lipschitz bound paired with the dimension factor in spherical concentration gives uniformly bounded moments of any higher order, hence uniform integrability. The convolution and third-moment identity follow from the folded normal. Expanding c_d^2 and g near r=0 gives limiting variance coefficients 1−3/pi, 1−2/pi and 0, so the quadratic converges uniformly on the closed interval. Its unique minimizer is the stated strict interior point, which also yields the eventual interior finite minimizers. The simulation is not relied on.
